styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Mughal forts, tombs and Old Delhi lanes.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street chaat, kebabs and butter chicken.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Bazaars, crafts and big air-conditioned malls.

stays.why: Cheapest beds, walk to New Delhi station and the Metro, and a short ride to Old Delhi. Busy and noisy streets.
Central, walkable and on the Yellow and Blue lines. Good for first-timers who want shops and cafés nearby.
Next to the airport with the Orange line link. Best for short layovers or early flights, far from the sights.
Mid-range hotels, a big shopping street and its own Metro stop. Lively and good value.

food: Start with street chaat: golgappa, papdi chaat and aloo tikki. Pick busy stalls and eat freshly made food.
Old Delhi is the kebab and paratha heartland. Try a paratha lane breakfast and seek out a famous kebab shop.
Order butter chicken or dal makhani at a classic North Indian restaurant. Book ahead on weekends.
Vegetarian thalis are cheap and filling, often ₹150–400. Many places are pure veg.
Drink only bottled or filtered water, and skip ice and cut fruit from street carts if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Day trip to Agra for the Taj Mahal: early train or a hired car with driver, roughly 3–4 hours each way. Check timings on the day.
Swap a city day for Humayun's Tomb, Qutub Minar and Lotus Temple in south Delhi, all on the Metro.
Add a half-day to Chandni Chowk spice market and the Red Fort, then rest in a haveli café.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Red Fort, Old Delhi food lanes and a south Delhi monument day. Add a night for an Agra trip.

month_notes: January: cold mornings around 8°C, mild afternoons near 19°C. Pack a jacket and expect fog delays.
February: pleasant and warming, highs near 24°C. Great month for walking the sights.
March: hot afternoons near 29°C, still comfortable mornings. Start sightseeing early.
April: hot at 36°C. Do monuments before 10am and rest indoors at midday.
May: very hot, highs near 39°C. Plan air-conditioned sights and evening outings only.
June: hot and humid at 38°C with more rain days. Carry water and expect sticky evenings.
July: monsoon peak, about 23 rain days. Expect heavy showers and flooded lanes; keep plans flexible.
August: still wet, around 19 rain days. Rain cools the air but streets stay messy.
September: rain easing to about 11 days. Humid but improving late in the month.
October: drier and cooler at 32°C. A strong month for sightseeing and festivals.
November: mild and clear, highs near 27°C. One of the best months to visit.
December: cool days near 21°C and cold nights around 9°C. Bring warm layers.

climate_guide.summary: Delhi has hot summers, a wet monsoon from July to September, and cool, dry winters. October to March is the comfortable window.

items.title: Best time: October to March
items.text: Mild days around 19–32°C and cool evenings. Ideal for forts, bazaars and long walks.

items.title: Summer is brutal (April to June)
items.text: Highs of 36–39°C. Sightsee at sunrise, then stay indoors or in the Metro at midday.

items.title: Monsoon (July to September)
items.text: Up to 23 rain days in July. Short heavy downpours, humid air and slow traffic. Carry a light rain jacket.

items.title: Winter fog
items.text: December and January mornings can be foggy, which delays flights and trains. Build in buffer time.

items.title: Cold nights in winter
items.text: January lows near 8°C. Bring a warm layer for evenings; many hotels have weak heating.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton for summer, a rain jacket for monsoon, warm layers for winter. Modest clothing for temples and mosques, plus comfortable shoes.

transit.best: Delhi Metro for most trips; ride apps for late nights and the airport.

modes.text: Cheap, air-conditioned and fast. Fares ₹10–60, more on the Airport Express. Nine lines; Yellow and Orange lines serve New Delhi station.
DTC and Blue-Line buses are frequent and very cheap, ₹5–25, but crowded.
Uber and Ola work well. Use prepaid taxi booths at stations and the airport to avoid haggling.
Driving is chaotic. Hiring a car with a driver is common for day trips.
Central New Delhi is fairly walkable with footbridges and subways. Use care crossing busy roads.
